items.explanation: Today. A special reading that belongs to the whole word, not to each kanji.
items.mnemonic: Kyō: 'Key, oh! Today I lost my key.'

items.explanation: Tomorrow. Formal speech uses あす. The plain present form 行く also talks about the future.
items.mnemonic: Ashita: 'Ash, eat a big breakfast tomorrow.'

example.reading: あした がっこうに いく。

items.explanation: Yesterday. 寒かった is the past form of 寒い: い-adjectives make their past with かった.
items.mnemonic: Kinō: 'Kino? No, I went to the cinema yesterday.'

example.reading: きのうは さむかった。

items.explanation: Every day: 毎 (every) + 日 (day). Also 毎朝 (every morning), 毎晩 (every night).

example.word: 毎日日本語を勉強する。
example.reading: まいにち にほんごを べんきょうする。
あさ コーヒーを のむ。
example.meaning: I drink coffee in the morning.

items.explanation: Noon, daytime; also short for lunch (昼ご飯).
items.mnemonic: Hiru: the sun is high at noon.

example.reading: ひるに ともだちと あう。
example.meaning: I meet a friend at noon.

items.mnemonic: Yoru: 'Your room is dark at night.'

example.reading: よるは ほんを よむ。

items.explanation: Now. いる says where a person is.
items.mnemonic: Ima: 'I'm a busy person right now.'

items.explanation: Time, and hours as a length: 二時間 (にじかん) is two hours, but 二時 (にじ) is two o'clock.
items.mnemonic: Ji-kan: 'Gee, can I have more time?'

items.explanation: This year. A special reading, like 今日 (きょう).
items.mnemonic: Ko-toshi: this year I'll finally go.

example.reading: ことし にほんに いく。
example.meaning: I'm going to Japan this year.
